observations: At shelf depth 50 cm, fixed back item reported reach 50 cm; slide-out position used 30 cm travel and reported 20 cm reach.
At depth 65 cm, slide-out reach rose to 35 cm with the same 30 cm travel.
Screenshots show the tray moving toward the shelf front with a reach line, but without a measured scale on the drawing.
Reveal describes depth minus travel, unchanged shelf volume, and horizontal-distance-only scope.
whyCool: You can bring a back item within reach without enlarging its shelf.
caveat: Schematic distance model, not a load or ergonomic assessment.
effort: Prediction, fixed and slide-out positions, deep-shelf boundary, screenshots and reveal.
bucketReason: Clear causal model despite an answer-revealing title.

prediction.reason: Title and labels give the answer.
prediction.evidence: Move the tray, shorten the reach.

interaction.reason: Mode and depth establish a controlled geometric comparison.
interaction.evidence: 50 versus 20 cm, then 35 cm at depth 65.

payoff.reason: Explains the operation and unchanged property.
payoff.evidence: Subtract travel from depth without changing shelf volume.

clarity.reason: Inputs, travel and reach are labeled.
clarity.evidence: Travel 30 cm, depth 65 cm, reach 35 cm.

transfer.reason: Concrete principle but limited guidance for a new situation.
transfer.evidence: Use trays within limits; models horizontal distance only.

visualExplanation.evidence: Tray moves toward front; no scale.

playfulness.reason: Two positions and variable shelf depth.
playfulness.evidence: Both positions and maximum depth tested.

practicalValue.evidence: Reach changes without shelf volume changing.
